text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds were little changed in late trading after a directionless day weighed upon by the market holiday in the U.S. Bund futures were down seven basis points at 103.58 in late afternoon dealings. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.63, up 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended in the red, easing back in trade muted by a holiday in the U.S. The market awaits a clutch of key data due later in the week. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-09/32, down 03/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled little changed after failing to break through Friday's close in a subdued session, hampered by the lack of price direction from the U.S. bond market, which was closed for a holiday. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.36, down 0.08 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets slithered into the doldrums in a subdued day and finished dragging their heels but above the day's lows. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.68, down 0.26 from Friday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - The U.S. Treasury market was closed for the Presidents Day holiday.

JAPAN - Japanese government bond futures ended the Tokyo session lower. Activity was limited due to a lack of fresh incentives. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.15, unchanged from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A holiday in the U.S. kept a lid on primary market activity, although a number of dollar deals were expected later in the week. Ford Motor Credit Corp will issue a $1 billion five-year global bond via Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers, the lead managers said in Hong Kong earlier. Launch was expected on Wednesday or Thursday and spread talk was in the mid- to high-30s basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, traders said. Also due later in the week was a $500 million five-year bond for Landesbank Rheinland-Pfalz.
